messages:
andrew: seeing p99 spikes and a few task errors on AMD nodes when seq_len > 2048. looks like selector didn't find a tuned kernel for the long-context path. might be an autotuner coverage gap.

serena: can you paste the failure log?

andrew: snippet below from the worker that failed the request: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:08:12Z] node=amd-gpu-07 model=fastchat-llama-seq seq_len=3072 route=autoselect
WARN kernel_registry: no tuned kernel for (arch=gfx906, seq_bucket=3072) -> using generic attention kernel
ERROR runtime.exec: kvcache eviction churn, task timed out after stall
```

kai: that WARN means registry didn't map that seq_bucket to any optimized kernel variant on gfx906. our autotuner job only covered up to 2048 in the last run (to save run-time).

marta: interesting — production traffic for a few customers has shifted to 3k+ contexts. autotuner config intentionally capped sampling, but we didn't realize traffic changed.

andrew: quick repro: replayed a batch of long-context requests against an AMD serving node. generic kernel responds but p99 increased ~210ms and we saw KV cache hit rate drop 97% -> 83% during fallback window.

serena: so we have two failure modes: perf regression (latency) and cache eviction churn causing some timeouts. both from falling back to generic kernels.

kai: immediate mitigations we discussed:
- conditional routing: route requests with seq_len > X to a pool flagged for generic kernels (cheaper isolation)
- run targeted autotune sweep that includes sparse high buckets (e.g. 256, 1024, 2048, 3072, 4096) across representative models
- precompile/generate generic kernels on AMD images at boot so fallback isn't cold

marta: for autotuner: let's change from contiguous range scanning to stratified sampling across seq lengths and model families. we can parallelize short profiler runs to keep overall time low.

andrew: tested simple routing rule locally — routing seq>2048 to generic-amd-pool stabilizes p99 but cost delta ~1.5x. good stopgap.

serena: code sketch for conditional route (can we push this behind a feature flag?):
```
function select_pool(req) {
  if (req.seq_len > 2048 && !kernel_existsFor(req.arch, req.model, req.seq_len)) {
    return 'generic-amd-pool'
  }
  return 'default-pool'
}
```

kai: also proposing a new metric to detect these gaps: kernel_registry_miss_total{arch,seq_bucket} and alert on sustained >0.3% over 30m. we can backfill using recent traces to find hotspots.

marta: infra-side: create a bootstrap job to prebuild generic attention kernels on AMD images and drop into /opt/rdw/kernels so registry has them at startup. helps reduce cold fallback impact.

deploy-bot: created PR for the routing feature flag: GH #4589. CI queued.

ops-bot: incident ticket INF-2026-229 created and ops-team tagged.

andrew: action items recap: (1) roll feature flag to us-west as a canary for 2h (andrew), (2) autotuner sampling change + focused profilers for 3072/4096 buckets (marta + kai), (3) add kernel_registry_miss metric + dashboard (kai), (4) prebuild generic kernels in AMD boot images (infra).

serena: please post status updates in the ticket. I'll notify support about possible latency for affected customers.

andrew: starting canary now, will report results in ~30m :rocket:
